jobs.description:
Overview

Eight decades ago, we were founded not by business people or investors, but by a community of 23 friends connected by the shared belief that a life outdoors is a life well lived. Together, they formed a co-op around the purpose that guides us to this day – to inspire and enable life outside for everyone.

REI is seeking a Sr. Project Manager, Go-To-Market (GTM) to lead the execution of new retail design concepts across our fleet of stores, including pilot programs and full fleet launches. This role ensures that innovative brand expression and store design concept strategies are delivered on time, on budget, and to the highest quality standards. The Sr. Project Manager, GTM partners with Store Design, Store Planning, Visual Merchandising, Retail Operations, Construction, and cross-functional teams to manage complex projects from concept validation through rollout. This leader models and acts in accordance with REI’s guiding values and mission. Models and acts in accordance with REI’s guiding values and mission.

This role requires expert knowledge of Project Management practices. The Sr. Project Manager, GTM is responsible for programs with moderate-high risk, ambiguity, and budget complexity. They are responsible for important team goals where the strategy may not be defined. The ideal candidate applies advanced principles, theories, concepts, and strategic

thinking. They use a wide application of strategies, policies, and previous experience to determine a course of action and deliver results independently. They plan and schedule daily tasks to be performed in support of the go-to-market program and makes choices on work prioritization with minimal assistance.

Lead end-to-end project management for new design concept implementations, from pilot through full fleet deployment.
Develop detailed project plans, schedules, and budgets, ensuring alignment with strategic objectives.
Coordinate with internal teams (Visual Merchandising, Store Planning, Retail Operations) and external vendors to ensure timely delivery.
Track project milestones and provide regular status updates to stakeholders.
Monitor project progress, identify risks, and implement mitigation strategies to maintain timelines and budgets.
Manage pilot programs, gather feedback, and incorporate learnings into rollout strategies.
Oversee vendor engagement and ensure compliance with design intent and quality standards.
Provide status reporting and KPI tracking to leadership and stakeholders.
Ensure operational readiness and training for store teams prior to launch.
Drive continuous improvement in project delivery processes and tools

Responsibilities And Qualifications

8+ years of program or project management experience in retail or related field.
Proven track record in large-scale rollout and pilot program management.
Strong understanding of retail store development processes, including design implementation and construction coordination.
Advanced ability to develop and manage project plans, schedules, and budgets.
Familiarity with risk management and mitigation strategies for complex projects.
Excellent stakeholder management and cross-functional collaboration skills.
Strong written and verbal communication for reporting and presentations.
Ability to influence and drive alignment across diverse teams.
Ability to manage multiple concurrent projects with high ambiguity.
Skilled in pilot program execution, feedback integration, and scaling to full fleet.
Demonstrated ability to deliver projects on time, on budget, and to quality standards.
Commitment to process optimization and adoption of best practices.
Ability to identify and implement efficiency improvements in project delivery.
Fosters a strong mutually supportive work environment where people can do their best work.
Proficiency in program management tools (MS Project, Smartsheet, Workfront)
PMP or equivalent certification.

At REI, we believe the outdoors is for all

The Corporate Revenue Cycle Department is seeking a dynamic and talented Program Manager - Revenue Cycle - Patient Access.

Monitors and analyzes Patient Access processes and KPI performance, and works with the facilities for continued improvement using action plans, training, and site visits as necessary.

About the Role

IT Project Manager (Workplace & End User Computing) operates as a hands-on execution driver, working closely alongside our Delivery Leads. This role is responsible for planning, coordinating, and delivering end-user technology migrations and workplace deployment projects from initiation through to hypercare and BAU handover.
The successful candidate will operate with a high degree of independence in fast-paced, multi-stakeholder environments. Acting as the central delivery coordinator across internal engineering teams, external third-party vendors, and business representatives, the Project Manager ensures that laptop rollouts, M365 tenant-to-tenant migrations, and broader EUC initiatives are delivered on time, within budget, and with minimal disruption to end-user productivity.

Project Mobilisation & Planning

Translate workplace and EUC transition objectives into detailed, actionable project plans, workback schedules, and deployment waves.
Adopt and run project-level governance, daily/weekly stand-up rhythms, milestone tracking, and clear escalation paths across technical teams and vendors.
Coordinate with technical leads, SMEs, and third-party deployment partners to validate hardware inventories, user cohorts, application readiness, and migration prerequisites.
Identify early delivery blockers, map technical and scheduling dependencies, and manage smooth transitions into active rollout phases.

End-to-End Delivery & Execution

Drive day-to-day execution across laptop refresh/migration programmes, M365 tenant-to-tenant migrations (mailboxes, OneDrive, Teams, identity), and workplace technology deployments (e.g., meeting room AV, local networking, and site readiness).
Coordinate delivery activities across EUC engineering, identity/security, desktop support, logistics, and external managed service providers.

Partner with internal teams (including Procurement, Facilities/Real Estate, and IT Service Desk) to align hardware provisioning, site access, and end-user support capacity.

Build strong working relationships with business unit champions, site leads, technical engineers, and third-party vendors to keep deployments aligned with operational needs.
Facilitate regular working group sessions, cutover readiness reviews, and vendor accountability meetings to resolve bottlenecks quickly.
Own end-user communications and change readiness plans (T-minus comms, VIP white-glove scheduling, drop-in clinics), ensuring migration schedules and user impact are clearly understood.
Bring structure and operational rigour to fast-moving workstreams, proactively driving alignment where local site requirements or user profiles vary.

Governance, Tracking & Reporting

Maintain accurate, real-time visibility over project schedules, deployment wave metrics, risks, issues, and dependencies.
Provide concise, outcome-focused status updates and RAG reporting to Programme/Delivery Leads and senior stakeholders.
Document cutover runbooks, deployment lessons learned, and handover documentation to ensure smooth transitions into BAU IT support.

Proactively identify, track, and mitigate delivery risks, such as hardware supply delays, application compatibility issues, or user scheduling conflicts, driving issues through to resolution.
Escalate critical blockers promptly to Delivery Leads with clear options and practical recommendations to keep cutover windows on track.
Adapt deployment schedules and logistics dynamically when business priorities or site constraints shift.

Track project-level expenditure against approved budgets, monitoring hardware deliveries, vendor statements of work (SOWs), and deployment milestone burn.
Flag budget variances, scope changes, or timeline shifts early to Delivery Leads and Finance partners to support accurate monthly forecasting.
Work closely with Procurement and vendors to track asset deliveries, licensing allocations, and milestone-based vendor invoicing.

Demonstrated ability to operate independently and drive accountability across internal technical teams, third-party vendors, and business stakeholders.
Experience delivering projects within multi-site, federated, or M&A/divestment environments is highly advantageous.

About the Role

IT Project Manager (Workplace & End User Computing) operates as a hands-on execution driver, working closely alongside our Delivery Leads. This role is responsible for planning, coordinating, and delivering end-user technology migrations and workplace deployment projects from initiation through to hypercare and BAU handover.
The successful candidate will operate with a high degree of independence in fast-paced, multi-stakeholder environments. Acting as the central delivery coordinator across internal engineering teams, external third-party vendors, and business representatives, the Project Manager ensures that laptop rollouts, M365 tenant-to-tenant migrations, and broader EUC initiatives are delivered on time, within budget, and with minimal disruption to end-user productivity.

Functional Responsibilities

Project Mobilisation & Planning

Translate workplace and EUC transition objectives into detailed, actionable project plans, workback schedules, and deployment waves.
Adopt and run project-level governance, daily/weekly stand-up rhythms, milestone tracking, and clear escalation paths across technical teams and vendors.
Coordinate with technical leads, SMEs, and third-party deployment partners to validate hardware inventories, user cohorts, application readiness, and migration prerequisites.
Identify early delivery blockers, map technical and scheduling dependencies, and manage smooth transitions into active rollout phases.

End-to-End Delivery & Execution

Drive day-to-day execution across laptop refresh/migration programmes, M365 tenant-to-tenant migrations (mailboxes, OneDrive, Teams, identity), and workplace technology deployments (e.g., meeting room AV, local networking, and site readiness).
Coordinate delivery activities across EUC engineering, identity/security, desktop support, logistics, and external managed service providers.
Maintain strong delivery momentum across concurrent deployment waves, ensuring cutover checklists, user readiness tasks, and post-migration hypercare activities are rigorously closed out.
Partner with internal teams (including Procurement, Facilities/Real Estate, and IT Service Desk) to align hardware provisioning, site access, and end-user support capacity.

Stakeholder, Vendor & Change Readiness Management

Build strong working relationships with business unit champions, site leads, technical engineers, and third-party vendors to keep deployments aligned with operational needs.
Facilitate regular working group sessions, cutover readiness reviews, and vendor accountability meetings to resolve bottlenecks quickly.
Own end-user communications and change readiness plans (T-minus comms, VIP white-glove scheduling, drop-in clinics), ensuring migration schedules and user impact are clearly understood.
Bring structure and operational rigour to fast-moving workstreams, proactively driving alignment where local site requirements or user profiles vary.

Governance, Tracking & Reporting

Maintain accurate, real-time visibility over project schedules, deployment wave metrics, risks, issues, and dependencies.
Provide concise, outcome-focused status updates and RAG reporting to Programme/Delivery Leads and senior stakeholders.
Document cutover runbooks, deployment lessons learned, and handover documentation to ensure smooth transitions into BAU IT support.

Risk, Issue & Dependency Management

Proactively identify, track, and mitigate delivery risks, such as hardware supply delays, application compatibility issues, or user scheduling conflicts, driving issues through to resolution.
Escalate critical blockers promptly to Delivery Leads with clear options and practical recommendations to keep cutover windows on track.
Adapt deployment schedules and logistics dynamically when business priorities or site constraints shift.

Budget & Commercial Tracking

Track project-level expenditure against approved budgets, monitoring hardware deliveries, vendor statements of work (SOWs), and deployment milestone burn.
Flag budget variances, scope changes, or timeline shifts early to Delivery Leads and Finance partners to support accurate monthly forecasting.
Work closely with Procurement and vendors to track asset deliveries, licensing allocations, and milestone-based vendor invoicing.

Requirements and Qualifications

Professional Experience

Minimum of 3–5 years of hands-on IT project management experience, with a strong, proven track record of delivering laptop migrations, M365 tenant-to-tenant migrations, and broader EUC/workplace rollouts.
Proven experience managing end-to-end deployment lifecycles, including discovery, pilot waves, mass cutovers, and post-go-live hypercare.
Demonstrated ability to operate independently and drive accountability across internal technical teams, third-party vendors, and business stakeholders.
Experience delivering projects within multi-site, federated, or M&A/divestment environments is highly advantageous.

Technical & EUC Domain Knowledge

Solid practical understanding of End User Computing technologies, including Windows/macOS device management, M365 tenant-to-tenant migrations (and standard migration tooling concepts), Entra ID/Active Directory, and modern workplace collaboration tools.
Familiarity with hardware logistics, zero-touch vs. white-glove provisioning workflows, application compatibility testing, and IT Service Desk handover processes.

Project Management & Delivery Methodologies

Strong command of core project management practices, including schedule/wave planning, RAID log management, cutover runbook management, and vendor SOW tracking.
Relevant project management certification (e.g., PRINCE2, PMP, APM PMQ, or Agile/Scrum) is desirable.

Commercial & Organisational Literacy

Sound commercial awareness with experience tracking project budgets, vendor SOWs, and hardware/licensing milestones.
Detail-oriented and numerate, comfortable maintaining project trackers, deployment wave schedules, and financial burn logs.

Soft Skills

Strong communication, facilitation, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage effectively from floor-level support engineers and VIP end users to senior business stakeholders.
Pragmatic, self-starting problem-solver with a strong bias for action, ownership, and operational rigour.
